source_text: Doctores nostri temporis, frater beatissime, et nefariae quae adhuc fervet seditionis auctores ad hominum, quorum sanctis studiis uruntur, contumelias et exitium decreverunt per ruinam totius Ecclesiae pervenire; non intellegentes quantum his contulerint honoris, quorum ostenderunt gloriam nisi cum cattolica religione non potuisse convelli. Nam si quis aut liberum in hominibus arbitrium aut Deum esse nascentium conditorem dixerit, Caelestianus et Pelagianus vocatur. Ne igitur vocentur haeretici, fiunt Manichaei, et dum falsam verentur infamiam, verum crimen incurrunt; instar ferarum, quae circumdantur pennis, ut cogantur in retia, quibus quoniam deest ratio, in verum exitium vana formidine contruduntur
pass_a_gloss: Teachers of our time, most blessed brother, and authors of the wicked sedition which still burns, have decreed to come through to insults and destruction of the men by whose holy studies they are burned, by the ruin of the whole Church; not understanding how much honor they have conferred on those whose glory they have shown could not be torn away except with the catholic religion. For if anyone has said either that there is free decision in human beings or that God is the founder of those being born, he is called a Caelestian and a Pelagian. Therefore, lest they be called heretics, they become Manichaeans, and while they fear a false infamy they incur a true crime; like wild beasts which are surrounded with feathers so that they are forced into nets, who, since reason is lacking to them, are thrust by empty fear into true destruction.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS liber=free; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere
LS arbitrium=judgment, free decision; Blaise liberum arbitrium
LS conditor; Blaise God as maker from nothing

pass_b_english: Most blessed brother, the teachers of our time, the authors of the wicked upheaval that still rages, have decided to bring insult and ruin upon the men whose holy efforts burn them, even at the cost of the ruin of the whole church. They do not understand how much honor they have given those men: they have shown that their glory could not be torn down without tearing down the catholic religion with it. For if anyone says that human beings have free will or that God creates those who are born, they are called a Caelestian and a Pelagian. So, to avoid being called heretics, people become Manichaeans. While fearing a false accusation, they fall into a real offense. They are like wild animals surrounded by feathers so that they can be driven into nets: lacking reason, empty fear pushes them into real destruction.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Glossary default: arbitrium is the decision-power, not a later Augustinian/Reformation free-will locus.
Freedom to abstain is required for will and sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, De nuptiis et concupiscentia 2 / On Marriage and Concupiscence); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
kind: Julian excerpt in the intermediary document
